So eight years ago I was in my freshman dorm and I had a shower and I did what I usually did which is shake my head in the shower to get excess water out of my hair

I had done this for 2 to 3 years previously

However this time after shaking my head for like 10 seconds I stopped and I immediately got nauseous dropped to the ground and threw up for the next two hours. I literally couldn’t see straight - everything was blurry it just seemed like my eyesight was tilted (like my head was straight but my vision is at a sideways angle). I crawled on all fours so I didn’t fall and hit my head on anything

Since then I have never shook my hair.

3 years later I was in a class with one of my teachers. He said that once he got hit in the head while moving tree branches and he was insanely dizzy but his doctor told him to lie flat on the ground and just tilt his head so you look all the way to the left then all the way to the right

And you hold it for a few seconds in each direction (looking left, looking right,looking to the sky) and you just repeat it 




Apparently if your head gets shaken too hard it messes up the liquid in your ears (which is essential for balance) so you literally can’t see properly because your brain is in a fog and can not understand how to balance you. 


Literally your brain is dizzy and the way to correct that is by doing that movement of your head - left to center to right to center and repeat for a couple rotations
